card: Adds functional test cases in mempool_accept.py verifying that transactions with Taproot stack elements over 80 bytes or empty control blocks are rejected with bad-witness-nonstandard. Previously, no test verified the specific reject reason for either rule, and empty control blocks were not exercised at all. This ensures regressions in mempool standardness policy checks for Taproot are caught deterministically in CI.
changed_since_previous: Dropped the test case for spends with an annex, retaining only the test cases for tapscript stack elements over 80 bytes and empty control blocks.
evidence: Author notes in PR description: 'With the 80-byte check removed, feature_taproot.py failed on only 6 of the ten seeds I tried, and with the empty control block check removed it can't fail at all, since none of its spenders has an empty control block. Without that check the node segfaults reading control_block[0].'
problem: Taproot standardness rejection rules in IsWitnessStandard lacked explicit assertions for bad-witness-nonstandard. Removing the empty control block check caused no failures in existing tests because no test runner generated an empty control block, while removing the 80-byte check only intermittently caused test failures depending on test seeds.

risk.why: Only adds test assertions to a Python functional test script.

summary: Adds functional test cases in mempool_accept.py for two Taproot standardness policy rules checked in IsWitnessStandard: tapscript stack items exceeding 80 bytes and empty control blocks. The test mutates a reference P2TR script-path spend and asserts that testmempoolaccept rejects the transactions with bad-witness-nonstandard.
